known_limitations: The title page says “Data Structures and Algorithms in Javascript” and “Second Edition,” while the copyright page and EPUB metadata use “Data Structures and Algorithms with JavaScript”; the copyright page describes a March 2014 First Edition and a 2015-10-21 Second Release rather than a clearly identified second edition.

The source is a 2015-updated EPUB of a book first released in 2014; JavaScript implementation details are source-era and target a SpiderMonkey-based shell, with separate Node translations noted by the source.

No current Google Apps Script, Node.js, JavaScript runtime, repository, errata, API, quota, trigger, authorization, deployment, or service behavior was externally verified because the build was intentionally source-only and offline.
The source contains educational code listings and exercises; this package paraphrases concepts and does not reproduce full listings, full algorithms, or exercise solutions.

The source’s October 20, 2015 update note says the iterative Mergesort was removed and replaced with a recursive one, yet the EPUB structure still contains a “Bottom-up Mergesort” subsection; the inconsistency is preserved as a source limitation rather than silently resolved.

Apps Script, spreadsheet, R365, SevenRooms, Uber Eats, forms, dashboards, scorecard, restaurant, and warehouse records are explicitly marked low-confidence extensions and do not describe unseen current project code.
Performance records provide structural reasoning and test gates, not current quota numbers or guaranteed complexity for hosted service calls.
